subject: MAP & evaluation: Skybridge performance benchmarking plan and closure timeline
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: MAP kickoff: Skybridge performance benchmarking plan and proposed close timeline

Hi Sofia / team,

Thanks for the productive demo yesterday. Per our mutual action plan (MAP) I put together an evaluation-focused benchmarking plan so we can align on acceptance criteria and the close timeline. Attached: Skybridge_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones) and benchmarking-runbook.pdf (test procedure).

High-level proposal (3-week evaluation):
- Week 1 (Hosted baseline): measure steady-state latency and throughput on Redwood Hosted API using your prod-like traces (sanitized).
- Week 2 (Dedicated smoke + isolation): reserved pool tests to validate predictability under concurrent load and autoscaling behavior. Canary and stress ramps.
- Week 3 (Private validation): optional VPC/on-prem validation for network/residency and final regression checks.

Key metrics (for acceptance):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 generation latency (ms) for our standard 512-token prompt; TTFT (time to first token) and cold/warm distinctions.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and tokens/min aggregated across clients, steady-state and peak.
- Concurrency: sustained concurrent request targets (50, 200, 800) with tails and error rates.
- Predictability: variance and SLO attainment (target p95 < 350ms for hosted baseline; p95 < 220ms for Dedicated at committed concurrency).

Measurement notes and constraints:
- We'll run both synthetic and replayed traces; KV cache warmup and pre-warming steps are in the runbook.
- For fairness we'll disable continuous prefix batching for the baseline and then re-introduce batching for cost-latency tradeoff tests.
- We need a Skybridge SRE point-of-contact for the private deployment window.

Proposed dates: kickoff next Tue (2026-07-13), wrap and MAP review by Fri (2026-07-31). If this looks good, please sign off on the MAP sheet and I’ll schedule the kickoff.

Next steps (ask):
1) Confirm SRE contact and procurement owner for PO/contract.
2) Sign-off on acceptance thresholds in the MAP.
3) Approve the proposed dates or provide blackout windows.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sofia — welcome Raj, glad you can join.

Couple follow-ups / clarifications after syncing with our infra team (high level):

1) Dedicated sizing & cost: for the week-2 dedicated smoke we recommend a reserved pool equivalent to 4 x A100-80GB (or equivalent vCPU/FLOP profile) to validate p95 under the 800-concurrency ramp. Estimated incremental cost for the reserved week (one-time test window) will be ~USD 18k — I’ll provide an itemized quote to procurement.

2) Private residency: yes — Private validation runs with customer-controlled VPC keep logs and metrics within your network. We’ll provide the private control plane artifact and a checklist in the runbook.

3) Detailed test phases (concrete):
- Baseline (Hosted): 3x 60-min steady-state runs at 50/200/800 concurrency; measure cold vs warm TTFT (first-run after model load).
- Dedicated (Isolation/Autoscale): controlled concurrency ramps to 100%, 150% of target with pacing windows; verify autoscale thresholds (scale-up at 75% GPU utilization sustained 30s, scale-down after 3m idle).
- Private (Network & Ops): single end-to-end regression run using your prod trace; validate ingress egress through your VPC and confirm audit logs retention.

4) Acceptance thresholds (proposed):
- Hosted: p95 generation latency < 350ms; error rate < 0.5% at target concurrency; TTFT (warm) < 120ms.
- Dedicated: p95 < 220ms at committed concurrency with < 0.2% error rate.

5) Test harness: we’ll hand over benchmarking-scripts.tar.gz (contains our runner and trace adapters). The scripts support both replay and synthetic traffic; they emit token-level timestamps so we can compute TTFT and tail latency precisely.

Operational asks:
- Raj / Skybridge: confirm a single SRE contact for the private window and the procurement contact for PO issuance.
- Raj: please note any OCI/AWS region constraints (we default to us-east-1 for Hosted).

I’ll upload the itemized quote and HubSpot MAP record once you confirm procurement contact — linking the MAP record here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/companies/skybridge-ai (will update with milestones).

If there are no blockers I’ll schedule the 30m prompt-set/traffic-mix call for Wed 7/15.

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: technical measurement notes

Quick technical notes from infra (log of changes we’ll apply during tests):

- TTFT definition: measured from request accept at ingress to first token emitted by model (end-to-end at the client). We’ll record both server-side and client-observed TTFT.
- Batching: baseline hosted runs will disable continuous request coalescing; Dedicated runs will exercise batching profiles: 0ms, 10ms, 25ms batching windows to characterize cost vs latency tradeoffs.
- KV cache warmup: warm-run sequences will include two warmup iterations to populate KV caches and avoid cold-start artifacts.
- Autoscale triggers: scale-up at sustained 75% GPU mem or 85% util for 30s; fallback policy: automatic degrade to a smaller compatible model variant (if allowed by MAP) with notification to Skybridge.
- Measurement artifacts: each run will produce token timing CSVs, aggregated percentile reports, and a run summary JSON.

Thresholds we expect to validate (engineering guidance):
- Hosted: p50 ~ 90-140ms, p95 ~ 240-360ms depending on prompt length; TTFT warm ~ 80-130ms.
- Dedicated (4x80GB baseline sizing): p95 ~ 160-230ms at 800 concurrent requests when KV is warm.

I’ll be on the Wed 7/15 call to walk through the harness.

-Karthik
